name: Gene Loves Jezebel
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Two identical twins from Porthcawl took turns at the microphone, fought over every lead vocal, and ended up running two bands with the same name on two continents.

hero.by: The House of Dolls line-up, 1988. Photo: James Stevenson, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Michael loves Jay
eras.text: The Aston twins grew up fighting rugby boys in Porthcawl and landed in London's post-punk art scene in 1981. While everyone else wore black, they went for silk, scarves and two lead singers.

years.h: Michael Aston moves to London and starts a band called Slavaryan
years.p: Michael names it after the Joy Division-era fixation on Slavs and Aryans, then drops it as too dark. [[Jay Aston|e9b564c0-dfac-40a5-9185-aa8ca5fe9bc0]] and guitarist [[Ian Hudson|600ea4f6-e712-4bc9-8840-5c920e5e509a]] arrive from Wales and the three share a flat in Pimlico.
years.xp:
Drummer James Chater came from a family with a famous house: his grandmother owned the place where [[Led Zeppelin|678d88b2-87b0-403b-b63d-5da7465aecc3]] recorded parts of Led Zeppelin IV and Houses of the Holy. Steve Radwell played bass, and a run of guitarists came and went before Hudson completed the line-up.

Michael, the older twin by 15 minutes, still says it was his band first. Jay still says he co-founded it. Goldmine noted that both give identical accounts of everything else.

years.h: A misheard name goes on the poster for the ICA Rock Week
years.p: A filmmaker thought Jay had introduced himself as Jezebel. Michael's limp from a football injury made him Gene, after Gene Vincent, and a friend's line about the twins always sticking together did the rest.
years.xp:
Jay says the name was settled the day the poster for their debut at the Institute of Contemporary Arts was drawn. "We won't have a one word name, we'll have a long name," he told Goldmine, the opposite of [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] and [[Killing Joke|f5aca88c-e3c1-4bc2-af33-68a9a9f7b56a]].

Melody Maker's Steve Sutherland was at that first show and started writing about them. Situation Two, the Beggars Banquet imprint, offered a deal before the band had played a third gig.

years.h: "Shaving My Neck" becomes a Melody Maker Single of the Week
years.p: Situation Two put out a rough demo the twins were embarrassed by. The goths loved it, and it's still on goth compilations.

years.h: "Screaming (For Emmalene)" gets its screams from a friend
years.p: The screams on the second single come from Kymille Chambers, a friend of the band. It reached No. 18 on the UK indie chart.

years.h: Julianne Regan sings one BBC session, then leaves for All About Eve
years.p: [[Julianne Regan|ae7170de-f331-43ab-b022-4b1af84d863c]] had played bass, piano and backing vocals, and sat out a tour with Xmal Deutschland. After a David Jensen session for Radio 1 she left and later formed All About Eve.

yt: Live at the ICA, London, December 29, 1983
years.h: Promise opens with "Upstairs" and lands at No. 8 on the indie chart
years.p: The debut centres on a nine-minute run of "Screaming (For Emmalene)" into "Scheming", with the twins' tangled vocals, moans and bird cries on top.

eras.title: Two Welsh boys in Manhattan
eras.text: A New York trip with John Cale, a BBC session that went wrong and a label running out of patience. Then John Leckie made Immigrant for a few thousand pounds, and America started listening.

years.h: John Cale takes the band to New York, and a snowstorm takes the bassist
years.p: Two shows at Danceteria and a session with fellow Welshman [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]]. Bassist Steve Marshall's flight was grounded for two days, so Jay played bass himself.
years.xp:
They had opened for Cale at London's Victoria Venue, and he liked them enough to produce four songs. "I was the only one sober in New York, which tells you everything," Michael told Goldmine.

Beggars never released the session. Michael believes the tapes were wiped or lost.

years.h: A Peel session the band begged to cancel
years.p: Hudson had just fired bassist Steve Marshall, so Jay filled in again on a ramshackle John Peel session. Michael blames that day for the BBC never playing them.
years.xp: "We had told them that we weren't ready," Michael said. The BBC refused to reschedule. The session included "Waves", a song never released anywhere else, and "Five Below", an early form of "Immigrant". [[Peter Rizzo|cc4f33f8-0b7f-445d-97ab-02b846a5a3ee]] eventually took over on bass.

years.h: Beggars gives the band one more shot, cheap
years.p: After the Cale tapes, two versions of "Always a Flame" (one with Steve Harley) and nothing released, Michael went back to Beggars and asked to make a record for a few thousand pounds. A&R man Terry Hollingsworth called [[John Leckie|7388621b-7649-40e0-a98b-67ef14938d9d]].

years.h: Immigrant, produced by John Leckie
years.p: Michael still calls it his favourite: "a real triumph of will over circumstance." The sleeve credits drummer Marcus Gilvear, but [[Chris Bell|c7136eca-afef-4cdd-b3df-5090aed5cede]] played on it.
years.xp: "The Cow" went out as a single and reached No. 9 on the UK indie chart. Some American cassettes put "Desire" in the wrong slot, which caused a songwriting-credit argument between the twins thirteen years later.

years.big: Three songs learned, sixty dates booked
years.src: Goldmine · Louder · Wikipedia: Gene Loves Jezebel
years.h: James Stevenson joins mid-tour after Ian Hudson's breakdown
years.p: [[Ian Hudson|600ea4f6-e712-4bc9-8840-5c920e5e509a]] had a breakdown early in the band's first long American tour and was sent home. Former Generation X guitarist [[James Stevenson|05368179-b400-430a-9e79-86af610d5d4f]] flew out and learned the set on the road.
years.xp:
Michael told Goldmine that Hudson cut his wrists and tried to jump from a 16th-floor window, and that his solo song "Sorry" is an apology to a friend of Hudson's who blamed him. Michael had seen Stevenson in Hot Club with Glen Matlock and Terry Chimes and kept his name in mind.

Stevenson hadn't heard Immigrant, so he put it on during the flight. His first thought, he told Goldmine: "Oh my God, what is this?" For the first shows the band swapped lyrics around the few songs he knew. [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]] opened some of the dates.

years.h: The first "Desire" is Michael's debut as a producer
years.p: Recorded before the tour with Hudson on guitar, co-produced by Michael and Alvin Clarke. It reached No. 4 on the UK indie chart.

eras.title: Pin-ups in silk and satin
eras.text: Geffen licensed them for America, MTV played the videos and the twins became pin-ups, Michael blond, Jay purple-haired. The more polished the records got, the harder the brothers fought over them.

years.h: Michael wins the lead vocal on Jay's "Sweetest Thing"
years.p: Jay sang backing vocals on his own song and was furious about it. Stevenson isn't on the sleeve photo because he was already thinking of leaving.

years.h: Producer Gary Lyons has a heart attack halfway through Discover
years.p: Engineer Mark Dearnley finished it, grabbing hours in London and at Rockfield. It reached No. 32, the band's first UK top 40 album.
years.xp: Early copies came with a bonus live record, Glad to Be Alive, taped at a Nottingham show in March 1986. The band, on tour, never got to mix it.

years.cap: The band in One Two Testing magazine, October 1986
years.src: Louder · Goldmine · Wikipedia: Gene Loves Jezebel
years.h: Peter Walsh re-cuts "Desire (Come and Get It)" for America
years.p: Geffen wanted [[Peter Walsh|8821570c-fc1e-4dd6-81f5-130b9f161b6c]] on the song, with Bell back on drums. It went to No. 6 on KROQ in Los Angeles and onto MTV.
years.xp: Louder describes the twins becoming pin-ups, Michael "blond and shamanic", Jay "purple-haired and brooding". "I couldn't go anywhere without people pulling at my hair," Jay said.

years.big: On two songs of his own band's album
q: That album, The House Of Dolls, was awful.
years.h: Michael walks out of The House of Dolls sessions
years.p: Michael quit over the slick sound and the choice of Walsh as producer. He sings on "Message" and "Up There" and the single "The Motion of Love", then rejoined for the tour.
years.xp:
"That album, The House Of Dolls, was awful," Michael told Classic Rock in 2017. Jay's answer: the songs only sound commercial "because he had to be included on them."

Jay says the original plan was for him to leave, and that Michael misread the signals. Both say the label pushed hard: Jimmy Iovine threw out the band's mix of "The Motion of Love" and did his own.

years.h: "The Motion of Love" puts them on the Billboard Hot 100
years.p: It reached No. 56 in the UK and, in 1988, No. 87 in the US. "Twenty Killer Hurts" turned up in a club scene on Miami Vice.

years.cap: The five-piece band with both Aston twins
yt: Live on MTV's New Year's party, 1988
years.h: The House of Dolls tour, taped in Toronto
years.p: North America, South America, Japan, then Europe, with the twins elbowing each other off the front of the stage. Michael moved to Los Angeles afterwards; Jay stayed in London.
years.xp: The Toronto Concert Hall show came out years later on Stevenson's Pink Gun label as half of In the Afterglow. Goldmine found the twins' vocals lacking fire, and said it would have been hard to be in form on that tour.

eras.title: Jay's band now
eras.text: Michael quit for good and Jay kept the name. A $250,000 album, a Bowie support slot and a label that went bust on a Bowie record followed.

years.h: After a six-month break, Michael Aston quits for good
years.p: Writing sessions with producer Steve Brown went nowhere. Michael went solo; Jay, Stevenson, Rizzo and Bell carried on as Gene Loves Jezebel.

years.src: Goldmine · Louder · Wikipedia: Gene Loves Jezebel
years.h: Kiss of Life survives an earthquake and a $250,000 rescue
years.p: Sessions with Paul Fox in San Francisco were interrupted by the 1989 earthquake, then partly re-recorded in London with [[Tim Palmer|2322b9ca-c0b0-4c86-a58f-3c8dd73c208b]]. "Jealous" went to No. 1 on the US modern rock chart.
years.xp: Louder puts the cost of re-recording at $250,000. Jay was still angry at Goldmine nine years later about edits to "Evening Star" and a whole verse cut from "Jealous".

years.cap: Jay Aston, Pete Rizzo, Chris Bell and James Stevenson, 1990
years.h: The US tour with Concrete Blonde falls through; Bowie's Milton Keynes shows come instead
years.p: Jay later heard that Johnette Napolitano pulled out over an interview she believed had slagged off Concrete Blonde. The band opened two sold-out [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]] shows at Milton Keynes, then toured with Billy Idol.
years.xp: Jay told Goldmine he never said it and loved Bloodletting. Goldmine gives the Milton Keynes crowd as 60,000.

years.h: Robert Adam replaces Bell, by way of AC/DC's drummer
years.p: Robert Adam was staying with Chris Slade when Slade's wife, a fan, heard Bell had quit. As a 12-year-old delivery boy Adam had got drum lessons from Phil Collins.

years.src: Goldmine · Louder · Wikipedia: Gene Loves Jezebel
years.h: Savage signs Bowie, goes bust, and Heavenly Bodies goes with it
years.p: The band turned down Atlantic for Savage's bigger advance. The label collapsed while they were touring the US.
years.xp: "We needed the money, we were broke," Jay told Goldmine. He still calls Heavenly Bodies the band's best album, and hated the sleeve Savage gave it. Goldmine blamed the label's spending on Bowie's Black Tie White Noise.

eras.title: Back together, briefly
eras.text: The twins patched things up, shared a house in Los Angeles and toured as a pair. By the end of the decade there were two Gene Loves Jezebels.

years.h: Two new songs for a best-of, and Michael hates one
years.p: Avalanche asked for a compilation with new tracks, so Michael recorded in London with Jay and Stevenson. He refused to sing on "Body and Soul"; "No Sweat" he could live with.

years.h: The twins tour America together, and scream at each other in Portland
years.p: Michael picked the band, including Human Drama's Michael Ciravolo; they played Jezebel songs and each brother's solo songs. The next night in Seattle they were inseparable again.
years.xp: "It's amazing we even got out of L.A.; we're on the highway out, and we're screaming at each other," Jay said. Promoters offered far more money for Gene Loves Jezebel than for two solo acts, which raised its own arguments.

q: They erased all my songs, all my vocals.
years.h: Michael's vocals come off VII, and Jay sues over the name
years.p: Jay brought back Stevenson and Rizzo for VII; after a rift on the reunion tour, Michael started his own Gene Loves Jezebel. Jay, Rizzo and Stevenson sued; the suit was dropped after a long fight.
years.xp:
Michael's version: they "erased all my songs, all my vocals." Jay's: "They were all my songs." The full album with Michael's vocals later came out as The Doghouse Sessions.

"In many ways I regret doing that. But I was so angry," Michael told Classic Rock about fighting for the name.

years.h: VII and Love Lies Bleeding: two Jezebel albums in one year
years.p: Jay's band issues VII; Michael's US band answers with Love Lies Bleeding, then Giving Up the Ghost and Exploding Girls.

eras.title: Gene in America, Jezebel in Britain
eras.text: Lawyers drew the map: Michael's band is Gene Loves Jezebel in the US, Jay's in the UK. Jay nearly quit music, then came back with a crowdfunded record and a run of good reviews.

years.h: Michael sues his twin for trademark infringement
years.p: The suit named Jay, Stevenson, Bell and others. A 2009 settlement split the name by territory: "Jay Aston's Gene Loves Jezebel" in the US, "Michael Aston's" in the UK.

years.h: The Smashing Pumpkins bring Jay and Stevenson out for "Stephen"
years.p: At Brixton Academy, [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]] played the Immigrant song with Jay Aston and James Stevenson on stage.

years.h: Dance Underwater, funded on Pledge after 14 years
years.p: Jay had come close to quitting and was working for Apple in London. A 2010 call to sing on a Rolling Stones tribute pulled him back.
years.xp: "I was smoking two packs of Marlboro a day, drinking too much," he told Classic Rock. On the money: "It's a long way from half a million dollars on an album."

years.h: The Mountain Goats put the Jezebel story in a song
years.p: "Abandoned Flesh" on [[The Mountain Goats|9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef]]' Goths runs through the band's history, Wikipedia page included.

years.h: A Santa Ana judge rules for Jay's band on all five counts
years.p: Michael had sued again after Jay's band played its first US tour in ten years. Judge James Selna found for the defendants and ordered Michael to pay their legal fees.

years.h: Love Death Sorrow on Cleopatra
years.p: Goldmine's Dave Thompson wrote that Stevenson was playing "some of the most grandiosely incisive guitar of his life."

years.h: James Stevenson leaves after nearly four decades on and off
years.p: Stevenson had been Jay's guitarist since the 1985 American tour, apart from the mid-1990s.

sources.title: Louder: From goth glory to bad blood, the Gene Loves Jezebel story (Classic Rock, 2017)
